body: Apache Spark - A unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing
plain_description: Apache Spark processes massive datasets at lightning speed, turning raw data into actionable business insights. It handles SQL analytics, machine learning, real-time stream processing, and graph analysis in a single unified platform. The bottom line: Make faster, data-driven decisions without waiting hours for batch jobs to finish.
technical_description: Apache Spark is a distributed computing framework and unified analytics engine for large-scale data processing. It provides high-level APIs in Scala, Java, Python, and R, backed by an optimized DAG execution engine that supports general computation graphs. Spark includes Spark SQL for structured data processing with DataFrames, MLlib for scalable machine learning, GraphX for graph processing, and Structured Streaming for real-time stream processing. It runs on Apache Hadoop YARN, Kubernetes, or in standalone mode, and integrates with HDFS, Hive, and other Hadoop ecosystem storage systems.
title: Apache Spark

body: The premier open source Data Quality solution
plain_description: The premier open source Data Quality solution. Profile, correct, and enrich your data to improve accuracy and trust. Use it for ad-hoc analysis, recurring cleansing, and Master Data Management.
technical_description: DataCleaner is a Java-based data quality toolkit for profiling, correcting, and enriching datasets. The modular architecture provides an engine core, a public API for custom extensions, and a Swing-based desktop UI. It supports job-based execution with configurable components for filtering, transforming, and analyzing data across databases, CSV, Excel, Hadoop, and other datastores.
title: DataCleaner

body: Code for the paper Hybrid Spectrogram and Waveform Source Separation
plain_description: Demucs separates any song into its individual components — drums, bass, vocals, and other instruments — with state-of-the-art accuracy. Musicians and producers can isolate stems for remixing, karaoke, or audio cleanup without needing a studio. The big picture: it's a free, open-source tool that delivers professional-grade source separation on a standard computer.
technical_description: Demucs is a music source separation library implementing Hybrid Transformer Demucs (v4), a U-Net convolutional architecture with cross-domain Transformer encoders operating on both spectrogram and waveform representations. It provides a CLI tool and Python API for separating audio into drums, bass, vocals, and accompaniment stems. The model supports GPU acceleration (minimum 3 GB VRAM) and CPU fallback, with processing time roughly 1.5x track duration on CPU. Pre-trained models include htdemucs, htdemucs_ft, htdemucs_6s, hdemucs_mmi, and MDX variants. Installation is via pip, with optional conda environments for training. The project is released under the MIT license and is no longer actively maintained.
title: Demucs Music Source Separation

body: DuckDB is an analytical in-process SQL database management system
plain_description: DuckDB lets you run fast, powerful SQL analytics directly on your data files without setting up a separate database server. Just embed it in your app or use the command-line tool to query CSV, Parquet, and JSON instantly. The bottom line: enterprise-grade analytics with zero infrastructure.
technical_description: DuckDB is an in-process, columnar SQL OLAP database engine implemented in C++17 with no external server dependency. It embeds as a library accessible via C, Python, R, Java, Swift, and Wasm bindings, executing vectorized queries directly against CSV, Parquet, JSON, and native storage formats. The engine features a full SQL:2011 dialect with window functions, complex nested types (arrays, structs, maps), nested correlated subqueries, and a pluggable extension system for Parquet, JSON, ICU, and full-text search. Integration supports zero-copy Arrow interchange and direct query pushdown.
title: DuckDB

plain_description: DVC lets your team version data and ML models the same way you version code. Track experiments, build reproducible pipelines that only re-run changed steps, and share results using Git plus your existing cloud storage — no servers needed.
technical_description: DVC is an open-source command-line tool for data version control and ML experiment management. It stores data and model artifacts in a content-addressable cache outside of Git, using DVC metafiles as placeholders within the repository. DVC pipelines define computational graphs that connect code, data, and model outputs, supporting incremental execution where only changed steps are re-run. The tool integrates with any cloud or on-premise storage (S3, Azure, GCS, SSH) and provides local experiment tracking with Git-based versioning, hyperparameter comparison, and visualization.
title: DVC

body: Flexible and powerful data analysis / manipulation library for Python, providing labeled data structures similar to R data.frame objects, statistical functions, and much more
plain_description: pandas is the must-have toolkit for anyone who works with data in Python. It lets you clean, transform, merge, and analyze datasets from spreadsheets, databases, and flat files — fast and without boilerplate code. The bottom line: if you need to make sense of tabular data, pandas saves you hours of manual work.
technical_description: pandas is a Python library that provides high-performance, easy-to-use data structures (Series and DataFrame) and data analysis tools. It implements labeled data structures with automatic alignment, integrated handling of missing data, a full-featured group-by engine for split-apply-combine operations, and time-series-specific functionality including date-range generation and moving-window statistics. The library supports robust I/O for CSV, Excel, SQL databases, HDF5, and Parquet, and integrates with NumPy for numerical computation. pandas is available via pip and conda.
title: pandas

body: Extremely fast Query Engine for DataFrames, written in Rust
plain_description: Polars is an extremely fast DataFrame query engine that processes analytical data dramatically faster than traditional tools. It handles datasets larger than your computer's memory through streaming, and comes with zero required dependencies for instant deployment.
technical_description: Polars is a multi-threaded analytical query engine for DataFrames written in Rust. It provides both lazy and eager execution modes with an optional streaming engine capable of processing datasets larger than available RAM. The library leverages the Apache Arrow columnar format and SIMD vectorization for high-performance data processing. Front-end APIs are available in Python, Rust, Node.js, R, and SQL, with a powerful expression API and query optimizer.
title: Polars

body: Vocal Remover using Deep Neural Networks
plain_description: Extract clean instrumental tracks from any song using AI — no studio required. Remove vocals from audio files for karaoke, video production, or music analysis with a single command. The tool runs entirely on your own machine, keeping your audio private and secure.
technical_description: vocal-remover separates mixed audio into instrumental and vocal tracks using deep neural networks implemented in PyTorch. The tool uses a deep U-Net convolutional architecture for audio source separation. It runs inference on CPU or NVIDIA GPU, with optional test-time augmentation and a post-processing mask for improved separation quality. The package includes a training pipeline for users to train custom models on their own instrument/mixture datasets. The tool is distributed as a Python CLI application with dependencies managed through pip.
title: Vocal Remover
